title: Keep results-list rows, focus and selection alive across the live-scan refresh
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: observed: Ctrl+Enter on the focused 'reading-row' row after one live refresh executed on [], expected exactly one execution on 'reading-row'. After the refresh: keyboard focus on ListBox (DataContext null), list SelectedIndex -1, Ctrl+Enter CanExecute from the focus False.
Derived 1 -- A live-scan refresh keeps the results list's rows and their item containers alive: it diffs or preserves items instead of replacing TopLevelList.ItemsSource wholesale: missing
Derived 2 -- Keyboard focus on a results row survives a live refresh (it stays on that row's container): missing
Derived 3 -- Selection of a results row survives a live refresh, including a row the tracker rebuilt as a new TopLevelRow object: missing
Derived 4 -- Ctrl+Enter on the focused results row after a live refresh opens that row (CanExecute true, executes exactly once on that row): missing

stable-collection-move-keeps-row-focus: Move loses r05's focus whenever r05 itself is Moved: S3 0/10 and S4 3/10 pass; S1, S2 10/10

real-showtoplevel-inplace-plus-refocus-passes-repro: needs first: Decide how a reorder keeps the focused row's container, or whether 'same container instance' is required at all, before building. Also decide how the repro test and the other readers of TopLevelList.Items address wrapper items.

Whether Q-078's window case is worth building as a person-run R-001 step plus a hook step, given that no loop stage can run it and lesson #340 says each WindowCases.ps1 edit draws a new finding. The practice designer built it because the person asked for it in Q-078. Nobody argued the other side.

Whether OnCanOpenInExplorer and OnOpenInExplorer should fall back to TopLevelList.SelectedItem when keyboard focus is on the list itself. Two lines would close the out-of-view, Cancel-race and return-from-Explorer gaps. It was left out to keep to Q-078's scope and to leave the shared gesture handlers alone, and it is filed as a follow-up.
R-001 step 16 was not run: it opens and closes real Explorer windows and is person-run (lesson #336). The hook step it uses was run unattended through a refusal-only variant instead.

WindowMutants -Mutant All (Q-114), the default Core suite, C-052, and the network pass are validate's. I ran the SL-100 and SL-063 projects, the architecture rule tests, the rules harness clean scenario, and L-001, L-002 and L-003.
Derived criteria 1 and 5 (containers kept alive; the Tag/CommandTarget pattern no longer needed) are not built, by decision Q-078.
SC-181's by-hand clicks and Alt+Tab-and-back with a real foreground switch, and the hardware-key gap SC-254, are the person's.
No loop-run L-case or WindowMutants mutant for the restore (finding m4, deferred to the standing-guard follow-up).

Standing guard for the SL-100 Facts, preferred shape from m4: a loop-runnable L-case (focus a row, wait 3 refreshes, Flush, log focused Path, SelectedItem Path and CanExecute, press with a PreviewExecuted handler marking it Handled) plus a NoFocusRestore mutant in WindowMutants.ps1; the hook's top-key step and the Hidden-folder tree with FSA_HOOK_EXPLORER_VIEW=0|0 already show how to run it without opening Explorer.

Resolve TopLevelList.SelectedItem in OnCanOpenInExplorer and OnOpenInExplorer when the focus is on the list itself (m8). This is the only thing that fixes a stopped list after a menu close or re-activation, and a focused row pushed out of view; it flips corpus rows F02, F05 and F08, which pin the measured dead press today.

Decide whether to keep `UpdateLayout()` and the stale-array guard in ShowTopLevel's Loaded callback: no test observes either (mutants M3 and M4 survive, and the probe shows the swap leaves the scroll offset and containers in place by Loaded). Both were kept because the design says so.

The interop exemption: either keep the two new except_files entries, or press Ctrl+Enter in the hook via cmd.Execute(null, focusedElement) and move the test project's user32 calls behind one excepted file.

Keep-containers-alive (Derived 1 and 5), only if a later row action needs containers that live across refreshes (Q-078). Spike 1's 'fixsafe' variant (move the other rows past the focused one) is the starting point.

deviation: m7 said to add a capture branch for `IsActive && Keyboard.FocusedElement is null`. Measured, neither a closed row menu nor a re-activated window leaves null: both leave the focus on MainWindow itself. The branch is FocusIsAdrift: list, or (active window and (null or the window itself)). This is a wider trigger than the design's 'only from the list itself', and a refresh now also moves a focus the person left on the window's blank area onto the selected row.

deviation: ArchitectureRulesTests.InteropLivesOnlyInNative was red once the SL-100 tree was on disk: the repro stage's file already had two DllImports, and my Rig and hook step add six more lines. The design declared no architecture rules. I added exemptions for tests/bugs/SL-100-ResultsListRefresh/** and tests/window/FsaWindowHook/RevealMode.cs to both fitness.yaml entries of that rule and to its xUnit twin, and checked with the rules harness clean scenario (0 hits) and the 19 rule tests. A reviewer can alternatively ask for the hook press to use cmd.Execute(null, focus) and drop one exemption.
deviation: The restore trigger also needed the capture to read the selected row's Path for the adrift case (focusKey = selectedKey), which the design had only for the list itself.
deviation: The design asked for a 'FocusOutsideTheListIsNeverMoved' Fact on the Cancel button; per m2 it uses the Settings button because the Cancel panel is collapsed in the harness.
deviation: ResultsListRefreshTests.cs: the only edit is `public class` to `public partial class`, so the new Facts can share the repro's helpers. The Fact itself is unchanged.

As a result corpus row F11 (ClearFocus on an active window) expects focus to be TAKEN, the opposite of the design's original case-8 expectation.

critique missed: Finding m7 prescribed the repair branch `window.IsActive && Keyboard.FocusedElement is null && selectedKey != null`, and m8 prescribed a list-only SelectedItem fallback. Both rested on a recalled claim that a closed row menu or a re-activated window leaves an active window with null focus. The critique never asked to measure where focus lands before prescribing a condition. The build measured that both leave focus on MainWindow itself. The trigger had to become FocusIsAdrift (MainWindow.xaml.cs:422-423), wider than Q-078's scope, and m8's list-only form would not repair corpus rows F02, F05 or F08. A check: any critique finding that prescribes a Keyboard.FocusedElement condition must name the Fact that measures it.

critique missed: The design declared no architecture rules and no fitness impact. The repro file already on disk, and the Press technique every new Fact reuses (Ctrl set in the thread key state), add user32 DllImports under tests/. ArchitectureRulesTests.InteropLivesOnlyInNative and both fitness.yaml entries for that rule went red. The fix needed except_files entries for tests/bugs/SL-100-ResultsListRefresh/** and RevealMode.cs, and the fitness.yaml edit then forced the full 124-row rules harness (Q-026/Q-027) at validate. The critique did not ask which existing fitness rules the new test project's P/Invokes would hit.

critique missed: The design ordered the callback as scroll restore, then UpdateLayout, then ContainerFromItem, with a stale-array guard. It justified this with the recalled claim that realised containers belong to the pre-restore offset after the Reset. The build measured that the swap leaves the offset and containers in place by Loaded. UpdateLayout and the guard are unobservable (mutants M3 and M4 survive) and were kept only because the design said so. The critique accepted the recalled claim without asking for a Fact that fails without UpdateLayout.

critique missed: The design's contract and key decision say 'the restore never scrolls'. Its own outside_claims entry (recalled) says Focus() can shift the offset by up to one item for a partly visible row. The critique did not force the contract to state the one-row exception or require a Fact for the cut-off last slot. The doc shipped with the unqualified claim (docs/design/SL-100-results-list-refresh.md:27) and only a test comment (ResultsListShapeTests.cs:106) admits it.

code-review missed: Round 1 did not read the test harness's failure paths. Rig.ModalDialogAround (FocusReturnTests.cs:236-241) has no try/finally, and the Rig's UnhandledException handler marks every exception Handled (ResultsListShapeTests.cs:361-365). A throw in ShowTopLevel while the modal dialog is open skips dialog.Close(), so corpus rows F07 and F08 hang the acceptance command instead of failing it.

code-review missed: Round 1 passed the corpus without noticing that the `gap` flag on F02, F05 and F08 is read by no code, and TheCorpusUsesOnlyTheWordsItDefines does not tie it to `expect: press-dead`. A new dead Ctrl+Enter can be pinned as expected behaviour without being declared a gap. A check: assert per row that gap equals (expect == 'press-dead').

still unknown: Does a real Alt+Tab, or Explorer taking the foreground after Ctrl+Enter, leave focus on MainWindow itself, as the in-process SetActiveWindow/SetFocus simulation measured? The corpus rows F02 and F05 depend on it. Only a person's SC-181 run can answer it.

still unknown: Does a real hardware Ctrl+Enter whose WM_KEYDOWN lands between a tick's ItemsSource swap and its Loaded callback run after the restore (SC-254)? Every press so far was raised in-process, and the Input-priority ordering was shown only by Facts and spike 3.

still unknown: Does the wider FocusIsAdrift trigger take focus in any real flow the Facts do not cover, such as a person who clicks blank window area mid-scan on a real C:\ or D:\ scan? The published exe ran only on a synthetic 48,000-folder tree under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp.

still unknown: Does container.Focus() scroll the list by one row when the focused row sits partly visible in the viewport's last slot? No test pins it (SC-264). It is ordinary during a live scan, because the focused row's index changes with every resize.

still unknown: Does R-001 step 16 pass in a real person run that opens Explorer? Neither the step nor the real reveal after Ctrl+Enter has ever been executed, and lesson #340 says each WindowCases.ps1 edit draws a new finding.

went wrong: The design's recalled claim that menu-close and reactivation leave null focus was wrong. The build measured the Window itself and widened the restore trigger beyond Q-078's 'if the list had keyboard focus'. Only a model accepted that behaviour change (a refresh now takes a focus left on the window's blank area), and no person decided it.

went wrong: The recorded m8 follow-up named the wrong focus state in three places: the doc (docs/design/SL-100-results-list-refresh.md:78-80), the corpus bounded_by text and the builder's follow-up. Code review had to correct it, and the correction was waived to SC-263 instead of rewording three lines, so the wrong text is probably still in the shipped doc and corpus.

went wrong: Three code-review findings of real size were waived to the backlog: the unstated scroll exception (SC-264), the unread `gap` flag (SC-265) and the modal-dialog hang (SC-266). The shipped state includes a doc claim ('the refresh never scrolls') known to be false by one row, and an acceptance command that can hang if ShowTopLevel throws.

went wrong: Code review needed two rounds. The first passed the production fix and matrix but missed the test-Rig hang and the unread corpus flag. The adversarial second round found both and reproduced the hang.

went wrong: The design kept two pieces nothing can observe: the stale-array guard and UpdateLayout (mutants M3 and M4 survive), because its case-5 premise (containers belong to the pre-restore offset) did not hold in the harness. They are carried as unverified code.

went wrong: The design declared no architecture rules, yet the interop rule went red once the SL-100 tree was on disk. The fix touched fitness.yaml and ArchitectureRulesTests.cs, which added the all-scenario rules harness (124 rows) to validate.

went wrong: The default suite was 804 of 805 at validate because the builder's untracked scratch launcher (.taad-scratch/sl100-topkey-run.ps1) tripped AppArgumentTests. The builder's mutant script now resolves M0 to the fixed file, so the recorded 'M0 24 of 29 red' cannot be reproduced from it.

went wrong: The headline merged criterion (SC-181, real clicks against a live refresh) and the requested Q-078 window case (R-001 step 16, with a real Explorer reveal) were not run by anything. The only evidence is in-process Facts and a refusal-only hook run, and all 12 findings had only model triage.
